1wiirlv:217: Mountpoint S3's core design philosophy is "not trying to emulate operations that S3 cannot provide," but instead delivering optimal performance within S3's capabilities. This means actively giving up operations that S3's object model inherently does not support, such as random writes and rename, in exchange for higher sequential read/write throughput. S3 Files takes a completely different path — by introducing a fully managed cache layer, it rebuilds complete file system semantics on top of S3. These two designs represent two reasonable compromises under the fundamental contradiction of "object storage vs. file system"; neither is absolutely superior, it only comes down to scenario fit.
